currentContext.business: Wonderla Holidays Limited operates amusement parks across Kochi, Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Bhubaneswar, with a recent expansion into Chennai, each offering a balanced mix of thrill, water and family attractions supported by in-house capabilities in ride design and maintenance. The Company has evolved into an integrated entertainment platform extending beyond rides into hospitality, food and beverage, retail and event-led offerings, with the Bengaluru resort 'Isle by Wonderla' complementing the core park offering and contributing to non-ticket revenue. It serves a broad customer demographic of families, thrill-seekers and children through a mix of ticket and non-ticket monetisation, with growing adoption of online booking channels.

currentContext.strengths: Established brand recognition — strong brand recall, customer engagement and repeat visitation built over more than two decades of presence|Strategic locations across key metropolitan and high-growth urban centres, providing access to large and diverse consumer catchments|In-house ride design and engineering capabilities enabling cost efficiencies, faster maintenance, enhanced safety standards and faster project execution|Diversified revenue streams — a balanced mix of ticket sales and non-ticket offerings (F&B, retail, hospitality) that improves earnings resilience|Integrated stay-and-play model via premium hospitality offerings such as Isle by Wonderla, increasing per-capita spending opportunities|High asset quality and operational excellence from continuous investment in ride safety, maintenance and infrastructure, backed by daily multi-point inspections and independent third-party audits|Integrated digital and marketing capabilities, with a growing share of online bookings and data-driven customer engagement|Disciplined capital allocation and a scalable expansion model backed by a strong balance sheet
currentContext.strategies: Evolve from a pure amusement park operator into a broader leisure and hospitality platform built around memorable experiences|Unlock the full potential of the expanded five-park portfolio while creating richer and more engaging guest experiences, rather than pursuing scale for its own sake|Grow in a measured and financially disciplined manner, directing capital toward opportunities that strengthen the business over the long term|Evaluate future expansion opportunities with discipline, guided by strategic fit, return potential and long-term value creation|Premiumise and monetise the non-ticket layer — food and beverage, retail and value-added experiences — to lift Average Revenue Per Visitor|Use digital initiatives to make the guest journey, from booking and park entry to the in-park experience, more seamless and convenient|Reposition the hospitality asset: rebrand Wonderla Resort as 'Terrea by Wonderla', an earth-inspired urban resort adjacent to the Bengaluru park, extending a single day of thrills into a multi-day immersive stay|Build organisational capability for a five-park footprint through structured training in technical operations, safety, hospitality and customer service, and through leadership development|Maintain safety as the foundation of operations via standardised protocols, ride inspection schedules, preventive maintenance and continuous employee training, guided by ISO 45001:2018 and ISO 14001:2015|Build a more resource-efficient operating model through energy management, water recycling and reuse, and responsible waste practices, including evaluation of rooftop solar and renewable power sourcing|The Board recommended a final dividend of 20% on face value, i.e., Rs. 2.00 per equity share of face value Rs. 10 each, for the year ended March 31, 2026, subject to Members' approval at the 24th AGM; the Company follows a Dividend Distribution Policy formulated in compliance with Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations and published on its website. No transfer to the General Reserve was proposed for the year, leaving retained earnings available to fund the expansion programme. Paid-up capital increased only marginally during the year through allotment of equity shares on exercise of stock options under the Employee Stock Option Scheme, 2016. Qualified Institutional Placement proceeds are ring-fenced against stated objects — development of the Wonderla Chennai Park, Glamping Pods and ancillary service areas at Wonderla Bengaluru, refurbishment at Wonderla Resort Bangalore, a roller coaster ride at Wonderla Park Bengaluru, general corporate purposes and issue expenses. The Company availed no loans from Directors or their relatives during the year, and confirms all related-party transactions were in the ordinary course of business and on an arm's-length basis, with no material related-party transactions (i.e., exceeding 10% of annual consolidated turnover) undertaken during the year.
currentContext.expansion: FY26 was an execution year in which the footprint went from four parks to five. The Company commenced operations of its Chennai park during the year, executed within the defined timeline and capital outlay; in its initial phase the park reported early revenue contribution and positive operating performance despite launch-related costs, and management is adopting a phased ramp-up approach with a near-term focus on brand building and market development, expecting margins to remain below those of mature parks initially with gradual improvement as operations stabilise. Wonderla now brings together five amusement parks in Bengaluru, Kochi, Hyderabad, Bhubaneswar and Chennai, along with Wonderla Resort, the ISLE and a range of food, beverage and retail offerings. On the hospitality side, Wonderla Resort was rebranded as Terrea by Wonderla, an earth-inspired urban resort adjacent to the Bengaluru park; backed by an investment of approximately Rs. 18 crore, all 84 rooms were refurbished across three distinct themes with curated dining and recreational experiences including the Caribbean Whirl. Proceeds of the Qualified Institutional Placement are earmarked for capital expenditure on development of the Wonderla Chennai Park, expansion and development of Glamping Pods and ancillary service areas at Wonderla Bengaluru, certain refurbishment at Wonderla Resort Bangalore, setting up of a roller coaster ride at Wonderla Park Bengaluru, and general corporate purposes. Beyond the current build-out, the Company continues to evaluate expansion opportunities across select locations, indicating a visible pipeline of new park developments under evaluation, backed by a disciplined capital allocation approach and a scalable expansion model. Higher cost pressures during the year arose from the commissioning of the ISLE and the Chennai park.
currentContext.mdna: India's organised leisure and entertainment industry continues to present significant long-term opportunities, supported by favourable demographics, rising discretionary spending and an increasing preference for experience-led recreation|Domestic tourism continues to gain momentum, with Wonderla positioned to participate through its expanding portfolio, strong brand presence and differentiated offerings|Full-year operations of Wonderla Chennai and the continued ramp-up of newer assets are expected to provide important growth opportunities in the years ahead|Expansion of THE ISLE hospitality offering is expected to be an additional growth avenue|Higher Average Revenue Per Visitor, driven by deeper guest participation across attractions, hospitality and food and beverage platforms, and by the growing contribution of non-ticket revenue streams|Profitability in the year reflected higher depreciation and operating costs following the commissioning of Chennai and the expansion of THE ISLE hospitality platform|Bhubaneswar continued to mature steadily, while Bengaluru, Kochi and Hyderabad remained strong contributors to operational stability and cash generation|India demonstrated strong economic strength with GDP growth of around 7.7%, supported by robust domestic demand, rising disposable incomes and sustained infrastructure investments, while the global economy grew approximately 3.4%|Healthy operating cash flows, prudent capital allocation and a largely debt-free balance sheet provide financial flexibility to invest in new attractions and future expansion

risks.risk: Cost pressure from newly commissioned assets
risks.note: Management describes the year as one of achieving footfall and revenue growth 'while navigating higher cost pressures arising from the commissioning of the ISLE and Chennai park' — new capacity carries launch and operating costs ahead of a mature revenue base.

The Company recorded an exceptional item on account of the impact of the new labour code within total expenses for FY 2025-26, showing that statutory labour changes flow directly into the cost base of a people-intensive park operation.

Regulatory developments relevant to the amusement park and entertainment industry are treated as a standing Board-level topic, covered as a dedicated theme in the FY 2025-26 familiarisation programme for Independent Directors.

risks.risk: Information technology, cybersecurity and data governance
risks.note: IT systems, cybersecurity practices and data governance were a specific familiarisation topic for the Board during FY 2025-26, reflecting exposure as booking, ticketing and guest-data systems move online.

risks.risk: Execution and ramp-up risk on new market entry
risks.note: Board familiarisation during the year included dedicated updates on the Chennai park launch and its operational performance, indicating that the ramp-up of a newly opened park is an actively monitored watch-item.

risks.risk: Dependence on continued capital expenditure and funding
risks.note: Updates on capital expenditure and funding plans formed a distinct part of the Board familiarisation agenda, and QIP proceeds remain tied to specified capital-expenditure objects — a growth model that requires sustained reinvestment.

one-line thesis: Wonderla delivered a record Q4 with 32% income growth driven by the new Chennai park, though FY26 PAT degrew 25% due to a high base of deferred tax benefits in the prior year. The core narrative shifts to margin normalization (targeting 40% EBITDA) as Chennai matures and management navigates significant delays in securing Tier-1 land for the next wave of expansion.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 551.1 Cr (+14% YoY); Q4 Rev: INR 142 Cr (+32% YoY). EBITDA: INR 192.5 Cr (+12% YoY), Margin 31% (Q4: 32%). PAT: INR 81.7 Cr (-25% YoY) vs INR 109.3 Cr prior; decline due to INR 24.1 Cr deferred tax benefit in FY25 (one-off). Order Book: N/A (Service). Net Debt: Cash-rich balance sheet; specific net debt figure not disclosed but implied low/negative given 'cash-rich' commentary and INR 35-40 Cr sustaining capex only.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Optimistic for FY27 driven by full-year Chennai contribution. Margin: Targeting return to ~40% EBITDA historically achieved pre-expansion phase. Order Inflow: N/A. Capex: INR 35-40 Cr (sustaining) for FY27; no large greenfield capex planned until land deals close.
order book & pipeline: N/A - Service business model; growth driven by footfall capacity and new park commissions rather than traditional order book.
segment / subsidiary detail: Parks: Footfall 32.19 Lakh (+6% YoY); Q4 Footfall 8.79 Lakh (+30% YoY). Chennai contributed ~1.9 Lakh in Q4. Hyderabad footfall down 7% YoY due to weather/monsoon and school ban incidents. Resorts: Best-ever performance with improved occupancy; ISLE gaming pod driving incremental revenue.
growth verticals / optionality: Plan to add 5 new parks over next 5 years (2-3 likely to be announced/completed in this window); strategic shift from Tier-2 to Tier-1 cities (Mumbai, Delhi, Ahmedabad) causing land acquisition delays; Resort business expansion as adjacent high-margin vertical.
margins & cost dynamics: FY26 EBITDA margin compressed to 31% (vs historical 40%) due to Chennai launch costs, ESOP expenses, and Labor Code provisions. Depreciation expected to rise by INR 50-55 Cr in FY27 due to Chennai capitalization. Management expects margins to revert to 40% as Chennai scales and one-offs dissipate.
capex / expansion: FY27 guidance: INR 35-40 Cr (sustaining/upgrades like Sky Wheel, new coasters). CWIP of INR 102.9 Cr to capitalize in Q1 FY27. Large greenfield capex paused pending land deal finalization in Tier-1 cities.
capital allocation: Cash-rich balance sheet prioritizing organic growth; exploring asset-light models for new parks; no buyback or dividend specific guidance given, focus remains on funding future Tier-1 expansions once land deals conclude.
risks & watch-items: Land acquisition delays in Tier-1 cities; Weather variability (monsoons/heatwaves) impacting footfall; Regulatory hurdles (50-60 licenses required); Discretionary spend softness due to macro/geopolitical tensions; Water scarcity concerns (mitigated by own sources).
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic on operational metrics but conservative on guidance due to macro uncertainty; transparent about land deal delays; confident in long-term 40% margin potential and Chennai's maturity curve.
non-obvious takeaways: Management explicitly noted that repeat visitation is structurally low (2-3 year cycle) regardless of new rides, relying on fresh demographics (10-25 age group); Non-ticket revenue currently 30% but targeted to reach 50% in 4-5 years; Hyderabad underperformance partly due to a specific one-off ban on school groups (50k-60k loss).

themes.title: Hospitality & travel up-cycle
themes.need: Q1FY27 split hotels from airlines. INDHOTEL delivered a 17th consecutive record quarter - consolidated revenue INR 2,419cr (+15%), EBITDA INR 753cr at 31.1%, standalone occupancy jumping to 82% from 76% on a 41.8% standalone EBITDA margin, and asset-light management-fee income INR 168cr (+26%) - with management now framing the West-Asia war as a NET tailwind because outbound travel stays home; leisure RevPAR (Rajasthan/Goa) ran up high-20s. Airlines got the mirror image: INDIGO's EBITDAR margin collapsed from 28.0% to 15.6% on blended ATF of ~INR 140-150/litre versus INR 85-90 pre-war (fuel CASK +~80% YoY), leaving yield as the only defence. MHRIL shows domestic leisure premiumisation is real - Keystone average unit realisation +73% to INR 14.4 lakh on stable gross sales. LEMONTREE/CHALET/SAMHI/THELEELA ride the same occupancy-led room cycle; TRAVELFOOD/TBOTEK/DREAMFOLKS remain levered to airport PAX and B2B travel.
themes.driver: Occupancy-led (not rate-led) RevPAR compounding plus INDHOTEL's Ginger conversion cadence stepping 15->20->25->40 per quarter through FY27; for airlines the swing is INDIGO's guided Q2 PRASK growth of 'more than 25%' on flattish capacity against ATF cracks.

themes.title: Media, entertainment & out-of-home advertising
themes.need: Digital-content, music-IP licensing and an advertising-recovery cycle underpin media - TIPSMUSIC on music IP; ZEEL/ENIL/RADIOCITY/BTML on broadcast/content; HTMEDIA/DBCORP/HMVL on print + digital; SIGNPOST/BRIGHT-tier and UFO on OOH/cinema. Ad-spend revival is the near-term swing factor.
themes.driver: Festive ad-spend recovery; music-licensing/streaming monetization; OOH inventory uptake.
